risk_reasons: A public, deliberately unrate-limited statutory opt-out endpoint performs durable database writes.
Adding a third Postgres client changes the application connection budget against the shared Supavisor and Postgres ceilings.
The worker's webhook and job capacity must remain available during a valid-token replay burst.
goal: Isolate one-click unsubscribe redemption behind a dedicated, tightly bounded Postgres client so valid-token replays cannot consume the shared worker pool used by webhooks and jobs.
non_goals: No rate limit, semaphore rejection, admission-control rejection, or other shed path for well-formed unsubscribe requests.
No change to token validation, redemption transaction semantics, response-status mapping, or per-token single-flight behavior.
No replay cache; its value and invalidation contract require a separate decision.
No schema migration, remote migration, deployment, environment-variable change, or production operation in this feature run.
No interface refactor of redeemUnsubscribeToken; ticket #652 owns making that function open its own transaction.
user_visible_behavior: A well-formed unsubscribe POST still returns 200 only after its durable redemption transaction commits, including concurrent same-token replays.
A burst of distinct valid unsubscribe-token redemptions uses the dedicated redemption pool and leaves the shared worker pool available for unrelated writes.
Malformed or unknown token behavior remains unchanged: malformed tokens open no database connection, and an unknown ledger token returns retryable 503.
invariants: A statutory unsubscribe request is never intentionally shed, throttled, or rejected because the redemption pool is busy.
The dedicated redemption pool has a fixed, reviewed bound and is independently admission-controlled at cap equal to its pool size, preventing Postgres.js pipelining wedges.

The client uses the same DATABASE_POOL_URL and therefore is local-slot isolation, not backend isolation; its capacity must remain within ADR-0009's 57 usable backend-session and 200 Supavisor-client constraints.
Invariant #15 remains intact: src/lib/db/server.ts owns client construction; worker ingress only consumes the exported composition-root client.
Each worker-owned dedicated Postgres client is closed during orderly shutdown.
Raw unsubscribe tokens are never logged, stored in a cache, or added to observability properties.
edge_cases: The redemption client is lazy, so importing src/lib/db/server.ts from Vercel code must not open a third connection unless the worker redemption path actually queries it.
A transaction failure on the dedicated client remains fail-closed as a 503 and reports through the existing sanitized error path.
Concurrent requests above the dedicated pool's local capacity wait rather than receiving a synthetic 503; the worker remains single-replica by invariant.
The existing same-token single-flight must call the dedicated client exactly once while preserving its capped bypass behavior for many distinct in-flight tokens.
The re-derived connection budget must account for Vercel's write pool (3), read pool (8), the new lazy redemption client, worker write pool (20), health client (2), and warm-isolate multiplication.

worker/ingress/unsubscribe.ts — HMAC gate, per-token single-flight, sanitized fail-closed path, and commit-before-200 contract.
worker/background/pollers/HealthAlertPoller.ts — narrowly scoped dedicated client lifecycle precedent.
docs/adr/0009-split-postgres-pools.md — measured ceiling, pool arithmetic, and staging burst-drill evidence format.
scripts/burst-drill-load.ts — existing staging worker-load drill harness and dedicated-client construction precedent.
test_seams: worker/ingress/__tests__/unsubscribe.test.ts through Fastify injection and mocked exported redemption client transaction boundary.
src/lib/db/__tests__/server.test.ts through exported client options, admission statistics, and shutdown lifecycle.
A bounded local burst-drill/test seam that holds redemption transactions while proving a shared sql write can acquire and commit.
tests_to_add: routes a well-formed one-click redemption through the dedicated unsubscribe client rather than the shared sql client
keeps malformed-token rejection before every redemption-client transaction attempt
admits only the reviewed number of concurrent redemption-client operations and queues excess work without a synthetic response
closes the redemption client during closeAllPostgresClients without weakening shared-client shutdown failure propagation
preserves the shared-pool write path while a bounded distinct-token redemption burst is in flight
pins the ADR-0009 capacity arithmetic and fixed redemption-pool maximum in the configuration contract
rollback_plan: Revert the application deployment before changing any environment configuration. The new client is code-only and lazy; reverting removes the dedicated pool and restores the previously verified shared-pool path without schema or data rollback. Do not raise any pool-size environment variable as part of rollback or release.
observability: The existing sanitized Unsubscribe redemption log remains the durable per-request outcome signal, with only outcome and hash prefix.
The staging burst-drill evidence records redemption-burst concurrency, unrelated-write availability, worker pool wait, and observed backend-session peak against the 57-session ceiling.
Client construction and pool bounds are mechanically pinned by db-server tests so a future size increase cannot silently invalidate the capacity calculation.
